raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
For Q1/Q2 with at most 16 KV splits, the row-per-warp combine launches four warps even though only one or two have rows. Launch 32/64 threads with an explicit 64-thread upper bound, reducing register allocation per block and improving residency. The kernel has no CTA barrier or cross-warp exchange, so its row mapping and arithmetic remain identical.

## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of LICENSE.txt.
- [x] Scoped `pre-commit run --files` passes.
- [x] Reviewed the applicable repository, Python, SDPA and test Hard Rules.
- [x] Labels include a change type, affected areas and originator.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / SDPA split combine.

## Summary

- Size the existing short-query combine block from its runtime query-row count; retain one shape-generic prepared entry.
- Extend artifact-reuse coverage across Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5 and the many-split boundary.

## Why

Local SM100 CUDA-event replay over four paged Q1/GQA8 length cohorts and split 1/2/4/8/16 shows a 2.6% aggregate full-attention latency reduction in both construction orders; the 16 changed split plans improve 3.2–3.3%. An independently compiled unchanged-source control moves within 0.04%. Including unsplit plans, the best tested one-long and mixed-length plans improve about 4.1–4.5% and 2.1%; equal-length cases continue to prefer the unchanged unsplit path. This is local kernel/graph-replay evidence, not a serving or other-GPU performance claim.

Paired profiling confirms 32 rather than 128 threads for Q1, unchanged registers per thread, and zero local spills. O and Stats are bitwise equal to the baseline in all eight profiled plans.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

No public API, plan selection, workspace, numerical policy, supported-feature or dependency changes. Other combine forms keep their launch geometry.

## Testing

- From `test/python`: `pytest -q -x -m L0 sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_split_combine_sm100.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_split_combine_many_splits.py` — 225 passed on SM100.
- Paired full-attention harness — 600 FP64 O/Stats checks covering initial execution, poisoned retained replay, fresh-pointer rebinding, old capture after rebinding and changed lengths, with both construction orders.
- Four targeted cases under each of `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --error-exitcode 99` and `--tool synccheck --error-exitcode 99` — all pass, zero errors. Cases cover runtime artifact reuse, live Q1, Q2/split16, and sink/padded rows.
- Six combine pointer forms each smoke-compiled for SM100/103/107/120 — 24 passed, PTX/CUBIN inspected. These are offline checks, not runtime qualification on the other GPUs.
- `pre-commit run --files python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/kernels/sm100/split_combine.py test/python/sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_split_combine_sm100.py` — passed.

detail.title: perf(sdpa): launch only live query warps in split combine

files.patch:
@@ -20,9 +20,11 @@
 partials are the same as a valid keyless row's, so the dense sink entry takes the per-batch Q lengths (``compile_ptr(has_q_lens=True)``) and drops the
 sink for those rows.
 
-One block of four warps per four (q_row, head, batch) rows, a lane owning four
-columns of d_v and walking the split axis; rows shorter than a block (decode,
-S_q < 4) take the decode form, whose four warps share one row's split axis.
+One warp per (q_row, head, batch) row, up to four rows per block; a lane
+owns four columns of d_v and walks the split axis. At S_q <= 2 the lean
+form launches only S_q warps, since there is no CTA barrier or cross-warp
+exchange. Past G_S splits, those short rows take the decode form, whose
+four warps share one row's split axis.
 
 The DECODE-GRID kernel (``_combine_decode_grid_kernel``), a fourth form of the
 lean fp32-partial path: one block per (q_row, head, batch,
@@ -2146,9 +2148,13 @@ def _launch_own_forms(
                 use_pdl=use_pdl,
             )
         else:
+            # One warp owns each query row, with no CTA barrier in this
+            # form.  Q1/Q2 need only one/two warps; the unused warps
+            # otherwise consume registers and limit resident blocks.
             _combine_kernel(*args, lean_wide=True, use_pdl=use_pdl).launch(
                 grid=((SQ + ROWS_PER_BLOCK - 1) // ROWS_PER_BLOCK, H, B),
-                block=[THREADS, 1, 1],
+                block=[cutlass.Int32(SQ) * cutlass.Int32(32), 1, 1],
+                max_number_threads=[64, 1, 1],
                 stream=stream,
                 use_pdl=use_pdl,
             )

@@ -130,7 +130,9 @@ def test_pointer_combine_reuses_artifact_for_new_shapes():
     owner = comb.compile_ptr(dtype_o="bf16", has_lse=True)
     fn = positional_entry(owner)
     assert fn is not None
-    for b, h, sq, d, splits in [(2, 3, 5, 160, 3), (1, 2, 3, 256, 5)]:
+    # One prepared entry changes between one, two and four query-row warps
+    # as its runtime shape changes, and retains the many-split decode form.
+    for b, h, sq, d, splits in [(2, 3, 5, 160, 3), (1, 2, 1, 128, 4), (3, 5, 2, 128, 16), (1, 2, 3, 256, 5), (1, 3, 1, 160, 17)]:
         op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
         ostride, lstride = _strides(b, h, sq, d, "strided")
         o, ostorage, oused = _output((b, sq, h, d), ostride, torch.bfloat16)
